issue: Marking the whole module optional is defensible for the conceptual framework and standard setting, which are not a 2026 FAR Blueprint group. But the module is also the only place on the platform that teaches two in-scope topics, so default-path learners (optional content excluded) are tested on material they are never taught: (1) the ASC 205-40 going-concern look-forward period and (2) how Codification references are built (Topic-Subtopic-Section-Paragraph and section numbers), which candidates need for research tasks.
evidence: Going concern: in-scope practice items far-nd-12, -13, -17 and -24 (far-notes-disclosures, not optional) test ASC 205-40. A grep for 'going concern' or '205-40' finds no hit in the far-notes-disclosures lesson, any other FAR lesson or content/far/review/*.md. The only teaching is the bullet in this optional lesson, plus far-cf-09 and far-cf-fc8. far-cf-09 and far-nd-12 are near-duplicates. Codification: seven in-scope FAR TBS have research parts (u1-income-statement, u2-analysis, u6-impairment, u9-construction, u10-fair-value, u11-operating-lease, x1-nfp). Only this lesson and far-cf-03 and far-cf-fc3 teach the citation format. far-tbs-u1-income-statement even lists far-conceptual-framework in moduleIds. Scope: blueprint-notes.md lists six verified FAR Area I group names (A for-profit, B NFP, C state and local government, D public company, E special purpose frameworks, F ratios), and none is a conceptual-framework group. A secondary 2024 CPA Evolution summary says '1.1 Conceptual Framework No longer tested' (https://www.scribd.com/document/715108309/CPA-Evolution-2024).
source: ASC 205-40-50-1; ASC 105-10; review/reference/blueprint-notes.md (FAR Area I groups); 2026 FAR Blueprint, Area I.A.6 notes (going concern disclosures)
fix: Keep the standard-setting and qualitative-characteristics sections optional. Move the going-concern bullet, expanded to cover the substantial-doubt-alleviated and not-alleviated disclosures, into the far-notes-disclosures lesson. Move the 'Finding your way around the Codification' section into an in-scope location (for example the far-notes-disclosures lesson or a non-optional research-skills note in far-exam-day.md). Re-home far-cf-03 and far-cf-fc3 (and far-cf-fc8) with it and set optional:false on them, or mark those sections and items non-optional.

issue: Skill and difficulty are overstated: the item is labeled analysis and difficulty 3, but it applies one definition (free from error) to a scenario whose stem already says the process was 'applied without mistakes'. That is application, or arguably remembering, at difficulty 2. It is the module's only analysis item and its only difficulty-3 item, so it distorts the skill mix.
evidence: The stem gives the decisive fact ('well-documented estimation process that was applied without mistakes'). The key restates the CON 8 QC15 definition. No relationships have to be analyzed and no data interpreted.
source: AICPA Blueprint skill definitions (Analysis = examine and study interrelationships; Application = use concepts to solve problems); CON 8 QC15
fix: Relabel skill: application, difficulty: 2. Or rewrite the item to need real analysis, for example two estimates where only one has a process error and the learner must decide which fails faithful representation.

issue: Answer cue and weak distractors. The stem's wording ('process that was applied without mistakes') is echoed by the key ('no errors in the description or process'). Distractors (b) 'can never be faithfully represented' and (d) 'exempt from the qualitative characteristics' are absolute and implausible, which leaves a two-option item: (a) vs (c).
evidence: Key (c) shares 'process' and 'error/mistakes' with the stem. (b) uses 'never' and (d) uses 'exempt'. No informed candidate would choose either.
source: Review brief section 2, per-MCQ check 6 (answer cues)
fix: Drop the 'without mistakes' clue from the stem; describe the process neutrally and let the learner judge. Replace (b) and (d) with plausible misconceptions, for example 'No, because estimates need only be verifiable, not free from error' or 'Yes, because the reserve must be adjusted retrospectively as an error correction'.

issue: Two distractors carry the trap label 'partial-computation' although neither involves any computation. far-cf-03 (a) '842-20-30' models confusing recognition with initial measurement. far-cf-08 (b) 'Materiality depends only on the dollar amount' models ignoring qualitative factors.
evidence: far-cf-03: the (a) explanation says 'Section 30 covers initial measurement — the amount — not whether and when to record'. That is a classification or wrong-rule error, and calc is false. far-cf-08: the (b) explanation says 'Qualitative factors ... can make small amounts material'. That is an overgeneralization or wrong-rule error.

issue: Absolutes appear only in distractors: (a) 'always immaterial' and (b) 'depends only on'. A test-wise candidate eliminates both without knowing the framework, which leaves (c) vs (d).
evidence: (a) 'Items under 5% of net income are always immaterial'; (b) 'Materiality depends only on the dollar amount'. The key (d) and distractor (c) have no absolutes.
fix: Reword without absolutes, for example (a) 'The framework sets 5% of pretax income as the materiality threshold' and (b) 'Materiality is assessed using quantitative factors, such as percentage of net income, rather than the nature of the item'.

issue: Option (c) 'Verifiability and understandability' is the only compound option. It clashes with the singular stem ('which ... is a fundamental qualitative characteristic'), so it is easy to eliminate on form. Its explanation covers only verifiability, not understandability.
evidence: Options: (a) Faithful representation, (b) Comparability, (c) Verifiability and understandability, (d) Timeliness. Explanation (c): 'Verifiability is an enhancing characteristic that supports faithful representation.'
source: CON 8 Ch. 3 (QC19-QC34 enhancing characteristics); review brief section 2, per-MCQ check 6
fix: Change (c) to a single characteristic, for example 'Understandability' or 'Conservatism' (trap outdated-rule). Make the explanation cover the option exactly.

issue: Near-duplicate of in-scope item far-nd-12 (far-notes-disclosures). Both have the same stem ('Under ASC 205-40 ... within what period'), the same key and the same 'one year after the balance sheet date' distractor. A learner who opts into optional content sees the same fact tested the same way twice, plus far-cf-fc8.
evidence: far-nd-12 stem: 'Under ASC 205-40, management evaluates whether there is substantial doubt ... within what period?' Key 'One year after the statements are issued'. far-cf-09 asks the same thing with key 'One year after the issuance date'.
fix: If going concern moves to far-notes-disclosures (see the coverage finding), retire far-cf-09 or rewrite it to test something new, for example whether 'available to be issued' applies to a non-SEC filer, or a scenario where the doubt is alleviated by management's plans.

issue: The lesson names the components of the qualitative characteristics only in a mermaid diagram and never defines them: predictive value, confirmatory value, completeness and the four enhancing characteristics. Practice item far-cf-04 tests the meaning of confirmatory value ('confirms or changes prior evaluations'), which the lesson never states.
evidence: The lesson body under 'Who are financial statements for...' defines only materiality and free from error ('Two traps the exam loves'). The terms Predictive value and Confirmatory value appear only as diagram node labels. far-cf-04 asks which component fits an analyst checking a prior-year forecast.
source: CON 8 Ch. 3, QC7-QC10 (predictive and confirmatory value), QC12-QC16 (faithful representation components), QC19-QC32 (enhancing)
fix: Add a short table under the diagram with a one-line definition and an example for each: predictive value (input to forecasts), confirmatory value (confirms or changes prior evaluations), complete, neutral, free from error, comparability, verifiability, timeliness, understandability.

issue: The recognition paragraph paraphrases CON 8 Chapter 5 (Recognition and Derecognition, August 2023) but cites only Chapters 1, 3 and 4. The lesson does not mention derecognition (also Chapter 5) or the Chapter 6 measurement framework, both eligible within the 2026 window per the reference sheet.
evidence: The lesson says recognition 'requires that the item meets an element definition, can be measured with a relevant measurement attribute, and can be faithfully represented'. These are the Chapter 5 criteria, and the citations list has no Chapter 5. far-standards.md §1c: Ch. 5 eligible from 4/1/2024, Ch. 6 from 4/1/2025.
source: FASB Concepts Statement 8, Ch. 5 and Ch. 6; review/reference/far-standards.md §1c
fix: Add 'FASB Concepts Statement No. 8, Chapter 5 (Recognition and Derecognition)' to citations. Optionally add one line each on derecognition and on Chapter 6's entry-price and exit-price measurement systems.

issue: 'Accrual basis — record revenues when earned' uses pre-ASC 606 'earned' wording. Revenue is now recognized when (or as) a performance obligation is satisfied, that is, when control transfers.
evidence: The lesson's 'Underlying assumptions' bullet. ASC 606-10-25-23 uses 'satisfies a performance obligation', and CON 8 Ch. 5 replaced CON 5's 'realized or realizable and earned' criteria.
fix: Reword: 'record revenues when performance obligations are satisfied and expenses when incurred, not when cash moves.'

issue: The explanation for distractor (a) calls 'one year after the balance sheet date' 'the older auditing reference point'. That period is still current under PCAOB AS 2415 for issuer audits, and IAS 1 uses 12 months from the end of the reporting period. Calling it old could mislead a candidate who also sits AUD.
evidence: The (a) explanation says 'That was the older auditing reference point'. PCAOB AS 2415.02 still uses 'a reasonable period of time, not to exceed one year beyond the date of the financial statements being audited'. The AICPA moved to the issuance-date period with SAS 132 (AU-C 570).
fix: Reword: 'One year after the balance sheet date is the IFRS (IAS 1) and PCAOB AS 2415 horizon; ASC 205-40 measures one year from the date the financial statements are issued (or available to be issued).' Consider trap 'wrong-rule' instead of 'outdated-rule'.

issue: Grammar and style mismatch: the stem refers to 'a private-company alternative' (singular), but the key begins 'They're available only to...'. That contraction is informal and has no plural antecedent.
evidence: Stem: 'proposes following a private-company alternative that lets entities amortize goodwill'. Key (a): 'They're available only to entities that aren't public business entities'.
source: Review brief section 2, per-MCQ check 6 (grammatical mismatch)
fix: Reword (a): 'Private-company alternatives may be elected only by entities that are not public business entities.'

issue: The overall explanation says 'Plans, internally generated reputation, and workforce skill fail...'. But option (a) is a signed purchase contract (an executory contract), not a plan, so the summary misdescribes the distractor.
evidence: Option (a): 'A signed contract to buy equipment in February; no payment or delivery has occurred'. The (a) explanation correctly calls it an executory contract, but the item explanation calls it a plan.
source: CON 8 Ch. 4 (executory contracts); lesson element table
fix: Change 'Plans' to 'Unperformed executory contracts' in the item explanation.

issue: The flashcard is not atomic. It asks for four separate facts (FASB, GASB, FAF, PCC roles) on one card, so a lapse on any one resets the whole card in spaced repetition.
evidence: Front: 'FASB vs. GASB vs. FAF vs. PCC — one line each'.
source: Review brief section 2 (flashcards: correct, atomic, unambiguous)
fix: Split into two to four cards, for example 'Which body sets GAAP for state and local governments?' and 'Does the FAF issue standards?', or keep it as a summary card but add atomic cards for the FAF and the PCC.

issue: Neither the Codification-navigation section nor the elements section has an inline check, although both are objectives. The only pre-question (pre1) primes elements, and the two checks cover the authority hierarchy and neutrality.
evidence: The lesson has ```check blocks for far-cf-chk1 (after authority table) and far-cf-chk2 (after QCs) only. Objectives 2 (Codification) and 3 (elements) have no check.
fix: Add a check after the Codification section (for example 'Where is the guidance on when to derecognize a financial asset? → -40') and one after the element table (for example a deposit received or an executory contract).
